title: A user field named __isArray__ converts its parent object into a JSON array
rationale: The worst manifestation of the same root cause and not mentioned anywhere in SECURITY.md. buildHierarchy places the decoded name as a real map key with value true; processArrays then evaluates its marker test on that user data and takes the array branch. The parent object does not merely lose a field - it changes JSON type.
catchesBugClass: Type confusion driven by field naming: the reconstructor reads control flow out of the same namespace it reads data from. Any consumer inferring a Spark schema gets array<struct> where the source had struct.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the __arrayPath__ twin, which is only removed and skipped so its failure mode is plain deletion. It also cannot tell you what happens when __isArray__ carries a non-true value.

predicted.detail: An object becomes an array and the __isArray__ field vanishes. Attacker-controlled key names can change the reconstructed JSON type, which is a schema-inference hazard, not just a fidelity gap.
